llm.summary: The skill is instruction-only and its requirements, instructions, and behavior are consistent with its stated purpose: it analyzes user-provided context to draft messages and explicitly says it never sends anything and requires user approval.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (relationship intelligence, detect signals, draft messages) match the SKILL.md, examples, and templates. The skill lists many signal sources (calendar, email, messaging, shared tabs) but as an instruction-only skill it does not request credentials or connectors — it expects the user to provide context. That design is coherent: connectors would require additional env vars and install steps, which are absent here.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions ask the agent to analyze potentially sensitive personal data (contacts, calendar entries, emails, messages, shared browser tabs) when that context is provided. The skill repeatedly cautions the agent to only cite sources actually available and never to invent access, and it explicitly states drafts are never sent without user approval. This is appropriate for the stated purpose, but it does mean the agent will be encouraged to process sensitive inputs if the user supplies them — users should avoid pasting credentials or private data unless they intend analysis.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files beyond templates and examples — lowest-risk model. Nothing is downloaded or written to disk by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths. Although it references external platforms (LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Gmail), it does not request access keys — consistent with an instruction-only skill that works from user-provided context.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (default) and disable-model-invocation:false (platform default). The skill does not request elevated or permanent system presence. Note: autonomous invocation is allowed by default on the platform — combine this with other installed skills that can send messages and you might create an end-to-end send flow; this skill alone does not contain sending logic.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and low-risk because it is instruction-only and asks for no credentials. Before installing, consider: 1) Privacy: the skill is designed to analyze sensitive contact/calendar/message data — only provide such data intentionally and preferably test with synthetic examples. 2) Sending: the skill says it never sends messages, but check your OpenClaw/agent environment for other skills or automations that can actually send messages (email, SMS, LinkedIn) so drafts can't be forwarded/sent without your review. 3) Connectors: because no credentials are requested, the skill cannot pull data from your inbox/calendar on its own — you'll need to supply context manually or via platform-managed connectors; confirm how those connectors are authorized. 4) Cultural risk: templates include culturally specific language; review drafts carefully before sending to avoid accidental tone or timing mistakes. If you want higher assurance, test the skill with anonymized/sample contact data first.
